question: In early July, a concert by DJ Barbara Butch in Grenoble was disrupted by pro-Palestinian activists ‘responding to a call for a boycott backed by LFI’1. In late July, an exhibition by the painter Bruno Chauvierre was cancelled by venue’s management on the grounds that the artist had been a Deputy of the French National Assembly for the National Front in 1986.

The artist refers to ‘possible pressure exerted on the event organiser by activists claiming to represent La France insoumise’2. The two artists’ profiles are different, but they have one thing in common. The far left is attempting to ban their performances because of their past or present political views, whether real or imagined. 1.
Is the Commission, which is spearheading the fight against discrimination, aware of these events?
Could it ask the competent French authorities to provide an assessment of the current state of affairs as regards violent extremist groups exerting pressure to censor artistic expression?
Can the AgoraEU programme provide funding for measures to support artists threatened by far-left extremist groups?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.11.2026) The Commission is committed to the values of respect for human dignity, equality and respect for fundamental rights1 and to supporting the rich diversity of the cultures of the Member States2, by carrying out actions to support, coordinate or supplement the actions of the Member States in the field of culture3.

The Commission recalls that by virtue of Article 167 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), culture remains a competence of the Member States. Freedom of expression and freedom of the arts are enshrined in Articles 11 and 13 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (the Charter)4.

According to its Article 51, the Charter is addressed to the Member States only when they are implementing Union law. In situations such as the ones presented by the Honourable Member it is for Member States, including their judicial authorities, to ensure that their fundamental rights obligations, as resulting from their constitutional order and international agreements, are respected.
Finally, regarding the AgoraEU programme, the proposal presented by the Commission in July 2025 is currently under negotiation in the European Parliament and in the Council.

Its proposed Creative Europe – Culture strand would be carried out in full respect for artistic freedom and diversity of cultural expressions and contribute to the improvement of working conditions for artists and cultural and creative professionals.

1 Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union, http://data.europa.eu/eli/treaty/teu_2016/oj. 2 Article 167(1) of the TFEU, http://data.europa.eu/eli/treaty/tfeu_2016/oj. 3 Article 6(c) of the TFEU. 4 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:12012P/TXT.
